claims.text: The starting material is an as-cast eutectic high-entropy alloy.
Tailored thermo-mechanical processing can introduce a lamellar microstructure into a eutectic high-entropy alloy.
The relevant lamellar microstructure consists of alternating soft FCC and hard BCC phases.
The processed microstructure retains a composite lamellar character while developing an ultrafine-grained duplex structure.
The lamellar microstructure produces a two-hierarchical constraint effect.
The processed microstructure generates a microcrack-arresting mechanism.
The two-hierarchical constraint effect and self-generated microcrack arrest improve the mechanical response during deformation.
Tailored thermo-mechanical processing that preserves lamellae can simultaneously improve strength and ductility in eutectic high-entropy alloys.
The intervention should produce high tensile ductility together with high fracture strength.
The improvement is expected relative to conventional eutectic alloys and high-entropy alloys lacking the tailored microstructure.
The proposed benefit should hold from room temperature up to 700 degrees Celsius.
The hypothesis is limited to eutectic high-entropy alloys with suitable compositions and processing conditions.
The exact relationship between lamellar structure and mechanical properties is not fully understood and may depend on alloy composition and processing conditions.
The hypothesis can be tested by comparing eutectic high-entropy alloys with and without the tailored lamellar microstructure.
Tensile ductility and fracture strength are the proposed response variables.
The hypothesis is falsified if the alloy without the tailored microstructure has similar or better tensile ductility and fracture strength.
